topic: Fundamental Constants and Mathematical Structure in Turbulence
target_audience: Advanced Undergraduate Physics or Engineering Students

sections.title: Introduction: The Challenge of Chaos (Duration: 45s)
lecture_lines: Turbulence is not chaos, but a structured hierarchy.
Energy cascades down through fluid movement scales.
Reynolds number defines the transition to turbulence.
animations: Large energy input visualizes as a bright orange (#FF8C00) vortex at center. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/vortex.svg]
Smaller eddies appear in cascading blue (#00BFFF) circles underneath.
Color-coded flow lines show energy transferring downward through layers.
Final tiny heat dissipation visualizes as subtle purple (#9370DB) particles. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/particles.svg]
Summary text 'Energy Cascade' appears in white (#FFFFFF) at top.

sections.title: The Kolmogorov Cascade: Mathematical Scaling (Duration: 1m 30s)
lecture_lines: Richardson proposed the energy cascade mechanism.
Large eddies break down into smaller ones.
Energy is dissipated as heat by viscosity.
Kolmogorov hypothesis defines universal scaling behavior.
Eta represents the smallest, final dissipation scale.
animations: High-speed large scale fluid motion appears as orange (#FF8C00) arrows [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/vortex.svg].
Large motion breaks into smaller green (#32CD32) swirling vortex regions.
Successive subdivisions continue to show fractal scaling, blue (#00BFFF) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/eddy.svg].

sections.title: The -5/3 Law: Spectral Analysis (Duration: 1m 30s)
lecture_lines: Energy spectrum E(k) distributes energy across scales.
Large eddies act as low-frequency bass.
Small eddies behave as high-frequency treble.
The power-law follows a negative five-thirds slope.
This slope confirms energy conservation in transfer.
animations: An energy spectrum chart appears with axis labeled 'k' and 'E(k)', featuring a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bass.svg] icon at the lower frequencies.
A slope line of -5/3 is drawn in bold red (#FF4500).
Data points align along the red slope to emphasize power law, indicated by a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/treble.svg] icon at the higher frequencies.

sections.title: Universal Constants & Dimensional Analysis (Duration: 1m)
lecture_lines: Universal constants remain constant across different fluids.
Dimensional analysis reveals hidden scaling laws.
Velocity fluctuations determine universal decay rates.
animations: The constant 'epsilon' appears, highlighting energy dissipation rate units near a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fluid.svg].
Variables 'k' and 'l' are arranged in a scaling dimensional equation.
The -5/3 coefficient is derived by balancing dimensional terms visually, illustrated by flow through a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pipe.svg].

sections.title: Conclusion & Real-World Application (Duration: 15s)
lecture_lines: These laws predict weather and atmospheric flow.
Aircraft design relies on turbulence scaling models.
Stellar convection follows these universal structures.
animations: Atmospheric weather map [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/weather.svg] shows turbulent kinetic energy zones, bright cyan (#00FFFF).
Zoom into an airplane wing [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/airplane.svg] showing air pressure turbulence, magenta (#FF00FF).
Final view returns to the initial cascading vortex, fading to white (#FFFFFF) with a sparkling star effect [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/star.svg].
